items.title: Why This Order? The Twelve Links Walked Through as a Single Lived Sequence

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，無明等諸有支作如是次第說？答：諸愚癡者要先愚於所應知事，次即於彼發起邪行。由邪行故，令心顛倒。心顛倒故，結生相續。生相續故，諸根圓滿。根圓滿故，二受用境。受用境故，若耽著，若希求。
items.en: Question: For what reason are ignorance and the other links taught in this particular order? Answer: One who is deluded must first be ignorant of what ought to be known, and only then, in consequence, undertakes wrongful conduct. Through wrongful conduct, the mind becomes distorted. Because the mind is distorted, rebirth is bound and continues. Because rebirth continues, the faculties become fully formed. Because the faculties are fully formed, both faculty and consciousness come to experience their objects. Because objects are experienced, one either grows attached to them or longs for them.

items.zh: 由希求故，於方覓時煩惱滋長。煩惱滋長故，發起後有愛非愛業。由所起業滋長力故，於五趣生死中苦果生。苦果生已，有老死等苦。謂內身變異所引老死苦，及境界變異所引憂歎苦熱惱之苦。是故世尊如是次第說十二支。
items.en: Because of this longing, affliction grows all the more in the very seeking of what is longed for. Because affliction grows, karma desirable or undesirable for a further existence is set in motion. Because of the growing force of this karma, a suffering result arises somewhere among the five destinies of birth and death. Once that suffering result has arisen, the suffering of old age and death follows — the suffering of old age and death brought on by change within the body itself, and the suffering of sorrow, lamentation, and distress brought on by change in the surrounding world. This is why the Blessed One teaches the twelve links in exactly this order.

items.zh: 復有次第差別，謂依二種緣建立緣起次第：一、內身緣，二、受用境界緣。內身緣，前六支所攝；受用境界緣，後六支所攝。
items.en: There is, further, a difference of sequence established by two kinds of condition: the condition of the inward body, and the condition of experiencing the outward world. The condition of the inward body is what the first six links belong to; the condition of experiencing the outward world is what the remaining six links belong to.

items.zh: 先於內身起我執等愚，由此不了諸業所引苦果異熟故，發起諸業。既發起已，即隨彼業多起尋思。由業與識為助伴故，能感當來三種苦果。謂根初起所攝苦果、根圓滿所攝苦果、受用境界所攝苦果。即名色為先，觸為最後。又於現法中，依觸緣受，發起於愛。由受用境界緣廣起追求，或由事業門，或由利養門，或由戒禁門，或由解脫門，發起欲求、內身求、邪解脫求。如是求時，令先所起煩惱及業所引五趣生死果生。既得生已，老死隨逐。
items.en: First, confusion such as self-grasping arises with regard to one's own body. Because of this, one does not understand the painful results, the ripening projected by karma, and so one sets karma going. Having set it going, one then thinks a great deal in accordance with that karma. Because karma and consciousness act as companions, they can bring about three kinds of painful result in the future: the painful result included in the first arising of the faculties, the painful result included in the completion of the faculties, and the painful result included in the experience of objects. That is, name-and-form comes first and contact last. Further, in the present life, feeling conditioned by contact gives rise to craving. With the experience of objects as condition, one pursues them widely, whether through business, through gain and honour, through precepts and observances, or through the pursuit of liberation; and so arise the search for sense pleasures, the search for existence, and the wrong search for liberation. Searching in this way, one brings about birth into the five destinies, the result of the afflictions and karma set going before. Once born, old age and death follow.

items.title: A Third Explanation: Three Kinds of Beings, Each Living Out a Different Portion of the Chain

items.zh: 復有次第差別，謂由三種有情聚。一、樂出世清淨，二、樂世間清淨，三、樂著境界。由初聚故，滅諸緣起，增白淨品。
items.en: There is, further, a difference of sequence founded on three kinds of beings: those who delight in transcendent purity, those who delight only in worldly purity, and those who simply delight in clinging to sense objects. Through the first kind of being, dependent origination is extinguished, and the pure, bright portion of the teaching increases.

items.zh: 由第二有情聚故，不如實知諸諦道理。若住正念，或作福業，或作有漏修所引不動業；若不住正念，便發非福業。或起追悔所引，或不追悔歡喜所引心相續住。彼又如前，於下中上生處，次第能感當來三種苦果，謂名色為先，觸為最後。
items.en: Through the second kind of being, the truths are not truly known. Abiding in mindfulness, one performs meritorious karma, or contaminated karma leading to meditative unmoving states; not abiding in mindfulness, one instead performs demeritorious karma. Just as before, in the lower, middling, or higher places of birth, this being brings about, in sequence, three future results — name-and-form first, contact last.

items.zh: 由第三有情聚故，依現受用境所生受，於現法中如前次第起後六支，謂受為先，老死為後。
items.en: Through the third kind of being, resting on the feeling arisen from presently experiencing sense objects, the remaining six links arise, in this very existence, in exactly the sequence already given — feeling first, old-age-and-death last.

items.title: Reciting the Chain Backward, and Why an Arhat's Liberation Is Named for Name-and-Form, Not Ignorance

items.zh: 問：何因緣故，逆次第中老死為先說諸緣起？答：依止宣說諦道理故，以生及老死能顯苦諦。
items.en: Question: For what reason, when the links are recited in reverse, is old-age-and-death spoken of first? Answer: This rests on the way the truths themselves are taught — birth and old-age-and-death are what make the truth of suffering visible.

items.zh: 如世尊言：新名色滅為上首法。問：何故不言諸無明滅為上首耶？答：依心解脫者而施設故。由彼於現法中種子苦及當來苦果不生而滅，故說名色為先，受為最後，得究竟滅。又於現法中受諸受時，愛及隨眠永拔不起說名為滅。由彼滅故，以彼為先餘支亦滅。
items.en: As the Blessed One said: the cessation of new name-and-form is the foremost teaching. Question: Why does he not instead say the cessation of ignorance is foremost? Answer: This is established from the standpoint of one who is liberated in mind. For such a one, the seed of suffering in this very existence, and the suffering result yet to come, no longer arises and thereby ceases — so it is said that name-and-form ceases first, and feeling last, reaching final cessation. And further, in this very existence, whenever any feeling is experienced, craving and its latent tendency are uprooted forever and do not arise — this is called cessation. Because craving thus ceases, every remaining link, taking it as the starting point, ceases as well.

items.zh: 如是等類，宣說緣起次第應知。
items.en: The order of dependent arising should be understood as taught in these and similar ways.

items.title: Why "Dependent Origination"? Five Layers of a Single Name

items.zh: 問：何故緣起說為緣起？答：由煩惱繫縛，往諸趣中數數生起故，名緣起。此依字釋名。復次，依託眾緣，速謝滅已，續和合生，故名緣起。此依剎那義釋。
items.en: Question: Why is dependent origination called by this name? Answer: Because, bound by affliction, one is again and again brought to arise among the destinies — this is what "dependent origination" is named for. This explains the name by its literal characters. Further: resting on a gathering of conditions, a thing swiftly passes away, and, resting again on a further gathering, continues to arise once more — this is what "dependent origination" is named for. This explains the name by its momentary nature.

items.zh: 復次，眾緣過去而不捨離，依自相續而得生起，故名緣起。如說：此有故彼有，此生故彼生，非餘。
items.en: Further: though the gathered conditions themselves have already passed, their influence is never abandoned, and a result arises resting on one's own continuing stream — this is what "dependent origination" is named for. As it is said: this existing, that comes to exist; this arising, that arises — and not from anything else.
The explanation of the names should be understood on the basis of this meaning.

items.title: Two Final Meanings of the Name — Endless Death-and-Rebirth, and the Buddha's Own Realisation

items.zh: 復次，數數謝滅，復相續起，故名緣起。此依數壞數滅義釋。復次，於過去世覺緣性已，等相續起，故名緣起。如世尊言：我已覺悟，正起宣說，即由此名展轉傳說，故名緣起。
items.en: Further: passing away again and again, and continuing to arise again and again — this too is what "dependent origination" is named for. This explains the name by its repeated arising and perishing. Further: having, in a past age, awakened to the very nature of conditioning, and then teaching it exactly as it was realised — this too is what "dependent origination" is named for. As the Blessed One said: "Having awakened to this, I now rightly proclaim it" — and it is by this very teaching, passed on from one to the next, that it is called dependent origination.

blocks.text: Today the treatise asks two questions about the twelve links: why are they in this order, and why is the teaching called "dependent origination"? The first answer walks through a single life as a lived sequence; the second gives the meaning of the name in seven layers.

subs.head: The order as a lived sequence

blocks.text: "One who is deluded must first be ignorant of what ought to be known, and only then, in consequence, undertakes wrongful conduct. Through wrongful conduct, the mind becomes distorted; through distortion, rebirth is bound." Venerable Miào Jìng: what ought to be known "is mainly one's own life, the six faculties and five aggregates, not mountains and rivers". The "distorted mind", both teachers say, is the last moment of the intermediate state, rushing towards its birthplace (Day 6).
The sequence rests on two conditions: the inner body, covered by the first six links, and experience of the world, covered by the last six.

The treatise also distinguishes three kinds of beings by how they live the chain. The first "extinguishes dependent origination and increases the bright portion". Master Cháng Bǎi: those training in the noble path, cutting the links through discipline, concentration, and wisdom. Others only continue it; others weaken it partly.

Why recite the chain backwards, starting with old age and death? Because of how the truths are taught: birth and old age and death make the truth of suffering visible. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Āgamas*: if beings had no ageing, sickness, and death, the Buddha would not need to appear in the world.

A sūtra says "the cessation of new name-and-form is foremost". Why not the cessation of ignorance? The treatise answers that this is said from the standpoint of one who is liberated in mind: for such a one, no new existence will arise. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Yujia lunji*: the seeds of name-and-form are the direct cause of the next birth; ignorance is only a remote condition. "New" contrasts with this life's "old" result.
The treatise gives seven meanings of the name 緣起:

items: By the literal characters: "bound by affliction, one is again and again brought to arise among the destinies." Venerable Miào Jìng: "like someone tied up and sent to prison; you must go whether you want to or not."
Things arise from conditions that are themselves passing away.
Past conditions are "never abandoned"; their force continues. Venerable Miào Jìng: the merit of a sincere repentance ceremony remains in the mind.
"This existing, that exists; this arising, that arises", "and nothing else". Venerable Miào Jìng: "else" means Brahmā and the unconditioned, which cannot be causes.
And finally, the Buddha "having awakened to the nature of conditioning, then teaching it". Venerable Miào Jìng: his own awakening is 緣; his teaching it to us is 起.

blocks.text: The last meaning is the most moving: the name of the teaching contains the act of teaching it. Dependent origination is not only how saṃsāra works; it is what the Buddha saw and then shared.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how does the explanation of the links' order begin?
options: the deluded first are ignorant of what should be known, then act wrongly, which distorts the mind, which binds rebirth
quiz.why: "One who is deluded must first be ignorant of what ought to be known, and only then, in consequence, undertakes wrongful conduct. Through wrongful conduct, the mind becomes distorted. Because the mind is distorted, rebirth is bound and continues." These map to ignorance, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, and so on.

quiz.q: What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "what ought to be known" mainly refers to?
options: mainly one's own life — the six faculties and five aggregates, not mountains and rivers
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "What ought to be known? The eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — not mountains and rivers, but mainly one's own life." Master Cháng Bǎi: the six faculties growing from name-and-form.

quiz.q: "Through wrongful conduct, the mind becomes distorted." Which moment's mind is this, according to the teachers?
options: the last moment of the intermediate state's mind — following one's karma, it is distorted and rushes towards its birthplace
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Put plainly, this distorted mind is the intermediate state's last moment." Master Cháng Bǎi: "This consciousness follows the karma done, distorting the intermediate-state mind so it rushes towards birth." The reading note's "at death" differs.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, why does the reverse sequence begin with old age and death?
options: it follows how the truths are taught — birth and old age and death reveal the truth of suffering
quiz.why: "This rests on the way the truths themselves are taught — birth and old-age-and-death are what make the truth of suffering visible." Master Cháng Bǎi: in the *Āgamas*, the Buddha says if beings had no ageing, sickness, and death, he wouldn't need to appear. Venerable Miào Jìng: it reveals life as suffering and inspires renunciation.

quiz.q: Why isn't "the cessation of ignorance" called foremost? What does the treatise answer?
options: it is set forth from the standpoint of one liberated in mind — future suffering never arises, and craving with its latent tendency is uprooted whenever feeling is experienced
quiz.why: "This is established from the standpoint of one who is liberated in mind. For such a one, the seed of suffering in this very existence, and the suffering result yet to come, no longer arises and thereby ceases." Venerable Miào Jìng: ignorance ceasing is wisdom-liberation; craving ceasing is mind-liberation.

quiz.q: How does the treatise explain the name by its literal characters?
options: bound by affliction, one again and again arises among the destinies — 緣 is being bound, 起 arising again and again
quiz.why: "Because, bound by affliction, one is again and again brought to arise among the destinies" — "This explains the name by its literal characters." Master Cháng Bǎi: "緣 is being bound by affliction; 起 is arising again and again among the destinies."

quiz.q: The final meaning: "having awakened to the nature of conditioning, then teaching it." How does Venerable Miào Jìng divide 緣 and 起?
options: the Buddha's own awakening is 緣; his teaching it to us is 起
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The Buddha's own awakening is called 緣; teaching it to us is called 起." "Equal" means what he taught equals what he realised. The preceding meaning, "passing away and arising again and again," refers to successive lifetimes.
